P1.headline: Steady fall on the same metformin. No drug was added.
P1.body: Mr. Dummy 1, 50, Patna. Dummy ABHA 91-2612-3348-1056. Five follow-ups from 03/12/2026 to 03/12/2027, all diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes. FBS 124 → 118 → 112 → 109 → 106. PPBS 178 → 165 → 154 → 148 → 142. HbA1c 6.5 → 6.3 → 6.1 → 6.0 → 5.9. Symptoms ease from reduced polyuria to asymptomatic. One dietary slip in March 2027 did not reverse the fall. Renal function is written as within range only on the second slip, with no number. The only medicine on every slip is metformin 500 mg, one tablet three times before meals. Diet and walking advice is repeated, not changed.
P1.watch: Nothing on these slips asks for a new drug. The next useful check the slips themselves name is a periodic HbA1c and a renal profile, which was not given as a number after visit 2.
P1.subtitle: ABHA 91-2612-3348-1056    prototype reading of these five slips only    not a clinical opinion

P2.headline: Glucose falls on unchanged metformin plus bedtime glargine. Proteinuria is the extra finding.
P2.body: Mrs. Dummy 2, 70, Gorakhpur. Dummy ABHA 14-7004-8821-5590. Five follow-ups from 04/08/2000 to 04/05/2001. First slip: home readings still high, FBS 158, PPBS 205, no symptomatic hypo, no HbA1c. Then FBS 142, 128, 120, 116 and PPBS 188, 176, 164, 158. HbA1c appears only from visit 3: 6.8, then 6.6, then 6.5. Visit 3 is the only slip that records urine protein still positive, and the diagnosis that day is Type 2 Diabetes with proteinuria. Later slips go back to Type 2 Diabetes and say monitor renal function, without a new protein result. Medicines do not change: metformin 500 mg, 1 × 3 before meals, and insulin glargine 10 U at bedtime.
P2.watch: The glucose line improved without a dose change. The open item is the protein: noted once, asked to be repeated, not repeated as a number on the later slips.
